To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we find a WTA-WTP gap that is robust across elicitation formats, but can be mitigated by using a payment elicitation format.

(1) the valuation method (i.e. contingent vs. inferred) has no significant effect on the WTA-WTP gap; (2) the payment format has a significant effect on the gap; and (3) the gap is significantly larger when a payment card is used as the payment format.

(i) we find a gap between WTA and WTP valuations, but (ii) the size of this gap can be muted using the payment card method, and (iii) we find a similar gap in valuations elicited using a contingent valuation or an inferred valuation method

the gap between the willingness to accept and willingness-to-pay for climate neutral foods.

there is a WTA-WTP gap for climate neutral foods that can be reduced by using the payment card format, and that the WTA-WTP difference does not vary with the elicitation method.
the elicitation method matters for the WTA/WPT gap, but that it is not a decisive factor in explaining the gap.

the WTP/WTA gap is a robust phenomenon, but that it can be muted by changing the elicitation format.

the WTA/WTA gap can be reduced by using a payment format that is less prone to framing effects.
